name: us-state-tax
description: Dependency-free US state AND LOCAL individual income tax engine for tax years 2025 and 2026, covering 28 states and 1,033 local income taxes. Models what rate tables leave out. VIRGINIA, whose four printed brackets are worth exactly $257.50 to every filer at every income forever, because the 5.75% top rate begins at $17,000 of taxable income for a single filer AND at $17,000 on a joint return and has since 1990 - so the Commonwealth's published $259 ceiling on the spouse tax adjustment is $1.50 above the largest figure its own worksheet can produce and has never once bound; where the age deduction is withdrawn DOLLAR FOR DOLLAR above $50,000 ($75,000 joint) of adjusted federal AGI, so a couple who are both 65 pay $2,760 of tax on $24,000 of income - 11.5%, twice the state's top rate, and a figure that appears in no table because it is two rules meeting; where that test reads federal AGI LESS taxable Social Security while the deduction comes off Virginia AGI, a gap worth $2,572.80 to a retired couple on $90,000; where a filer born on or before 1 January 1939 is not income-tested at all, so the provision sunsets by mortality; where TWO poverty floors set by two different governments mean the cliff is $168.55 for a single filer, $106.23 for a childless couple and $416.55 for a family of four - and vanishes entirely for the same family if they claim the federal earned income credit, because Virginia's 20% match and its $300-a-head Credit for Low Income Individuals are alternatives and only one is refundable; and where NO county, city or town levies an income tax at all. Ohio, whose printed schedule is DISCONTINUOUS - a filer with $26,050 of taxable nonbusiness income owes nothing and one with $26,050.01 owes $342.00, because O.R.C. 5747.02(A)(3) charges the constant whole on the first dollar of the band, so reading the three rows as marginal brackets understates every Ohio filer by $342 - and which steps a SECOND time by $18.69 at $100,000 because HB 96 re-based the lower constant from $360.69 to $342.00 and left the upper one at what $360.69 chained to; where the first $250,000 of business income is deducted and the excess taxed at a flat 3%, so $250,000 of Schedule C profit costs $0 and $250,000 of wages costs $7,022.45; where the exemption chart and every credit limit are read against a modified AGI that adds the business deduction straight back; where the $20 exemption credit is claimable ONLY by a childless single filer in a $1,550 window of income and the joint filing credit's 20% row is unreachable arithmetic; and where 679 municipalities charge 0.45% to 3.00% on QUALIFYING WAGES - box 5 of the W-2, which a 401(k) deferral does not reduce, costing a Columbus saver $612.50 a year that box 1 never shows - so the municipal tax is the LARGER half of every Ohio return below $126,408.32 of income, an Ohio retiree owes their municipality nothing, and a commuter pays the higher of the two rates whichever way they commute because Ohio has no statutory resident credit and no half rate for nonresidents; Michigan, where Detroit charges residents 2.4% on a base the MI-1040 does not contain, where the personal exemption has been the $600 the Legislature set in 1964 and is worth $14.40 against an indexed $5,800 state exemption, and where a Lansing resident commuting to Detroit pays 70% more city tax than one working at home; Indiana, where the average county rate is 1.914% against a state rate of 3.00%; MARYLAND, which TAXES SOCIAL SECURITY AND EXEMPTS PENSIONS - the state does not tax the benefit and then charges the whole of it, taxable or not, against the pension exclusion dollar for dollar, so $30,000 of benefits plus $60,000 of pension and $90,000 of pension alone reach the same Maryland AGI to the cent and a dollar of benefit adds a FULL dollar to the base while a dollar of pension adds nothing; where that exclusion is claimed PER PERSON so a return's totals do not determine its tax - one couple with $80,000 of pension and $40,000 of benefits pays $720.00, $758.40 or $3,261.65 depending only on whose name the income is in; where an IRA is NOT an employee retirement system, so the rollover every adviser recommends costs a retiree $3,428.03 a year at $150,000 with nothing on the federal return to show it happened; where military retired pay has NO age gate at all and the first $100,000 of a centenarian's income comes off whatever it is; where the maximum exclusion FALLS in 2026, the only parameter here that has ever gone down; where every resident owes a county income tax of 2.25%-3.30%, where Frederick County's bracket selects one rate that applies to the WHOLE income so one dollar at $150,000 costs $360.03, and where the new 2% capital gains surtax is a test rather than a floor so one dollar of AGI at $350,000 can cost $6,933.08; Massachusetts, which every rate table reports as a flat 5% and which taxes short-term capital gains at 8.5%; New Jersey, whose retirement exclusion ends in a wall that costs a joint retiree $1,381 on one dollar; CalEITC, which is a triangle with no plateau; New York City's 3.078%-3.876% resident tax and its 30%-to-10% sliding earned income credit; the Yonkers surcharge of 16.75% of the state tax; which federal figure each state starts from; which federal deductions it adds back; and the credit phase-outs that make Utah's and Pennsylvania's flat taxes anything but flat. Every figure cited to the statute or state release it came from, and every carried-forward figure flagged as provisional.
